51057.explanation:
\(f(x) = \frac{x}{3 - x} \)

f(x) has a defined value except at x = 3 where the function is undefined.

51121.question_text: If (x - 3) is a factor of \(2x^{2} - 2x + p\), find the value of constant p.
51121.explanation:
Using remainder theorem, since x - 3 is a factor, then 

given \(2x^{2} - 2x + p\), f(3) = 0

\(2(3^{2}) - 2(3) + p = 0 \implies 18 - 6 = -p\)

\(p = -12\)

51124.subject: Further Mathematics
51124.question_text: If \(\sin x = -\sin 70°, 0° < x < 360°\), determine the two possible values of x.
51124.explanation:
The value of the sine of an angle is negative in the third and fourth quadrant. Hence options A and B are not the options.

\(\sin 250 = -\sin (250 - 180) = - \sin 70\)

\(\sin 290 = - \sin (360 - 290) = - \sin 70\)

51130.subject: Further Mathematics
51130.question_text: For what values of x is \(\frac{x^{2} - 9x + 18}{x^{2} + 2x - 35}\) undefined?
51130.explanation:
An fraction is undefined when the denominator has value = 0.

\(\frac{x^{2} - 9x + 18}{x^{2} + 2x - 35}\) is undefined when \(x^{2} + 2x - 35 = 0\)

\(x^2 + 7x - 5x - 35 = 0 \implies (x + 7)(x - 5) = 0\)

\(x = \text{-7 or 5}\)

51135.subject: Further Mathematics

51142.subject: Further Mathematics
51142.explanation:
\(y = 2(2x + \sqrt{x})^{2}\)

Let \(u = 2x + \sqrt{x}\)

\(y = 2u^{2}\)

\(\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d u} = 4u\)

\(\frac{\mathrm d u}{\mathrm d x} = 2 + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\)

\(\therefore \frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = (\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d u})(\frac{\mathrm d u}{\mathrm d x})\)

= \(4u(2 + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}) \)

= \(4(2x + \sqrt{x})(2 + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}})\)

51146.subject: Further Mathematics
51146.question_text: Calculate, correct to one decimal place, the acute angle between the lines 3x - 4y + 5 = 0 and 2x + 3y - 1 = 0.
51146.explanation:
\(\tan \theta = \frac{m_{1} - m_{2}}{1 - m_{1}m_{2}}\)

\(m_{1} = \text{slope of 1st line } 4y = 3x + 5 \implies y = \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{4}\)

\(m_{1} = \frac{3}{4}\)

\(m_{2} = \text{slope of 2nd line} 3y = 1 - 2x \implies y = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{2}{3}x\)

\(m_{2} = -\frac{2}{3}\)

\(\tan \theta = \frac{\frac{3}{4} - (-\frac{2}{3})}{1 - ((\frac{3}{4})(-\frac{2}{3}))} = \frac{\frac{17}{12}}{\frac{1}{2}}\)

\(\tan \theta = \frac{17}{6}\)

\(\theta \approxeq 70.6°\)

51155.question_text: Find the axis of symmetry of the curve \(y = x^{2} - 4x - 12\).
51155.explanation:
The vertical line \(x = \frac{-b}{2a}\) is the axis of symmetry of the curve.

\(y = x^{2} - 4x - 12\)

\(\text{Axis of symmetry} = x = \frac{-(-4)}{2(1)} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\)

51156.subject: Further Mathematics
51156.question_text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve \(y = 4x^{2} - 12x + 7\) at point (2, -1).
51156.explanation:
\(y = 4x^{2} - 12x + 7\)

\(\frac{\mathrm d y}{\mathrm d x} = 8x - 12\)

At x = 2, y = 8(2) - 12 = 4

Equation of the tangent to the curve: \(y - (-1) = 4(x - 2)\)

\(y + 1 = 4x - 8 \implies y - 4x + 1 + 8 = y - 4x + 9 = 0\)

51161.subject: Further Mathematics
51161.question_text: The mean age of 15 pupils in a class is 14.2 years. One new pupil joined the class and the mean changed to 14.1 years. Calculate the age of the new pupil.
51161.explanation:
\(Mean = \frac{\text{sum of ages}}{\text{no of pupils}}\)

Let the sum of the ages of the 15 pupils be x and the sum of the 16 pupils be y.

\(\frac{x}{15} = 14.2 \implies x = 14.2 \times 15 = 213\)

\(\frac{y}{16} = 14.1 \implies y = 14.1 \times 16 = 225.6\)

\(\text{Age of new pupil} = 225.6 - 213 = 12.6\)

51165.subject: Further Mathematics
51165.question_text: The distance s metres of a particle from a fixed point at time t seconds is given by \(s = 7 + pt^{3} + t^{2}\), where p is a constant. If the acceleration at t = 3 secs is \(8 ms^{-2}\), find the value of p.
51165.explanation:
Differentiate distance twice to get the acceleration and then equate to get p.

\(s = 7 + pt^{3} + t^{2}\)

\(\frac{\mathrm d s}{\mathrm d t} = v(t) = 3pt^{2} + 2t\)

\(\frac{\mathrm d v}{\mathrm d t} = a(t) = 6pt + 2\)

\(a(3) = 6p(3) + 2 = 8 \implies 18p = 8 - 2 = 6\)

\(p = \frac{6}{18} = \frac{1}{3}\)

51169.subject: Further Mathematics
51169.question_text: The probabilities that a husband and wife will be alive in 15 years time are m and n respectively. Find the probability that only one of them will be alive at that time.
51169.explanation:
P(only one alive) = P(husband and not wife) + P(wife and not husband)

= m (1 - n) + n ( 1 - m)

= m - mn + n - mn

= m + n - 2mn

51179.subject: Further Mathematics
51179.question_text: In a class of 50 pupils, 35 like Science and 30 like History. What is the probability of selecting a pupil who likes both Science and History?
51179.explanation:
Let the number of students that like both Science and History = x

Number of Science only = 35 - x

Number of History only = 30 - x

35 - x + 30 - x + x = 50

65 - x = 50

x = 15

P(Science and History) = \(\frac{15}{50} = 0.30\)

51194.subject: Further Mathematics
51194.question_text: Find the least value of n for which \(^{3n}C_{2} > 0, n \in R\).
51194.explanation:
\(^{3n}C_{2} > 0 \implies \frac{3n!}{(3n - 2)! 2!} > 0\)

\(\frac{3n(3n - 1)(3n - 2)!}{(3n - 2)! 2} > 0\)

\(\frac{3n(3n - 1)}{2} > 0\)

\(3n(3n - 1) > 0 \implies n > 0; n > \frac{1}{3}\)

The least number in the option that satisfies \(n > 0; n > \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\)

51226.subject: Further Mathematics
51226.question_text: Find the direction cosines of the vector \(4i - 3j\).
51226.explanation:
Given \(V = xi +yj\), the direction cosines are \(\frac{x}{|V|}, \frac{y}{|V|}\).

\(|4i - 3j| = \sqrt{4^{2} + (-3)^{2}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\)

Direction cosines = \(\frac{4}{5}, \frac{-3}{5}\).

51229.subject: Further Mathematics
51229.question_text: Yomi was asked to label four seats S, R, P, Q. What is the probability he labelled them in alphabetical order?
51229.explanation:
The number of arrangements for the 4 letters = \(^{4}P_{4} = \frac{4!}{(4 - 4)!}\)

\(4! = 24\)

Alphabetical order is just 1 of the arrangements for the letters 

= \(\frac{1}{24}\)

51239.subject: Further Mathematics
51239.question_text: Two particles are fired together along a smooth horizontal surface with velocities 4 m/s and 5 m/s. If they move at 60° to each other, find the distance between them in 2 seconds.
51239.explanation:
Given lines \(OA\) and \(OB\) inclined at angle \(\theta\), the line \(AB\) is gotten using cosine rule.

\(|AB|^{2} = |OA|^{2} + |OB|^{2} - 2|OA||OB|\cos \theta\)

\(|AB|^{2} = 4^{2} + 5^{2} - 2(4)(5)\cos 60\)

= \(16 + 25 - 20\)

\(|AB|^{2} = 21 \implies |AB| = \sqrt{21}\)

\(\implies \text{The two particles are} \sqrt{21} m \text{apart in 1 sec}\)

In two seconds, the particles will be \(2\sqrt{21} m\) apart.

51249.subject: Further Mathematics
51249.question_text: A bicycle wheel of diameter 70 cm covered a distance of 350 cm in 2 seconds. How many radians per second did it turn?
51249.explanation:
Given:
- \( d = 70 \, \text{cm} \)
- \( D = 350 \, \text{cm} \)
- \( t = 2 \, \text{s} \)

Circumference: \(C = \pi d \approx 219.91 \, \text{cm}\)

Rotations:  \(\text{Rotations} = \frac{D}{C} \approx 1.59\)

Radians: \(\text{Total radians} = 1.59 \times 2\pi \approx 9.98\)

Angular Velocity: \(\omega = \frac{9.98}{2} \approx 4.99 \, \text{radians per second}\)

 \( \omega \approx 4.99 \, \text{rad/s} \) ≈ 5 rads

51258.subject: Further Mathematics
51258.question_text: The initial velocity of an object is \(u = \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} ms^{-1}\). If the acceleration of the object is \(a = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} ms^{-2}\) and it moved for 3 seconds, find the final velocity.
51258.explanation:
\(u = \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} ms^{-1}\)

\(a = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} ms^{-2}; t = 3 secs\)

\(v = u + at \implies v = \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} \times 3\)

= \(\begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 9 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -9 \end{pmatrix} ms^{-1}\)\)
